3  JUDGMENT 1.
The claimants are in appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

2. The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation ('K.S.R.T.C.', for short), is also, in appeal contending that there was no negligence on the driver of its bus, and therefore, the Corporation is not liable to pay the compensation.

3. It is not in dispute that as a result of the motor vehicle accident which occurred on 08.03.2017,
Girish, a 38 year old died.
4.
It is the case of the K.S.R.T.C. driver that the deceased suddenly crossed the Road and this resulted in the accident.

Admittedly, the accident occurred on a National Highway and having regard to the fact that the driver of the bus had a clear vision of the road, it has to be held that he was responsible for the accident.
It is also to be noticed here that the police, after investigation have laid a chargesheet against the driver of the K.S.R.T.C. bus.
More importantly, the K.S.R.T.C. itself is holding a departmental enquiry against the driver of the K.S.R.T.C. bus.
The Tribunal has noticed these facts and has come to the conclusion that the driver of the K.S.R.T.C. bus alone was responsible for the accident.
I find no reason to interfere, and therefore, the same is dismissed.

4. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence adduced before it, has thereafter proceeded to award the following sums as compensation:
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 12,15,000/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 40,000/-
 3. Loss of estate 15,000/-
 Transportation of dead body and  4. 15,000/-
 funeral expenses

5. In order to arrive at the loss of dependency, the Tribunal has determined the monthly income,
notionally at Rs.9,000/-.

Since there is no credible evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income,

sentences.text:
it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2017, would be Rs.11,000/-.
6.
Since the deceased was aged 38 years and was self employed, 40% requires to be added to the monthly income towards future prospects, which would result in the income to be Rs.15,400/-.

As the dependants are five in number, th is to be deducted towards his personal expenses, and hence,
his monthly income would be Rs.11,550/-.
7. The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the 'loss of dependency' would thus be Rs.11,550/-.
8. As the deceased was aged 38 years, the appropriate multiplier of '15' would have to be applied.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,79,000/- (Rs.11,550/- x 12 x 15)
towards 'loss of dependency'.
9.

The claimants being the widow, sons and parents of the deceased, they would each be entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/- towards 'loss of consortium' i.e., in all Rs.2,20,000/- and they would also be entitled to a sum of Rs.33,000/- under the 'conventional heads'.

10. Thus, the claimants, in modification of the impugned award, would be entitled to the following sums :
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. (In Rs.)
 1. Loss of Dependency 20,79,000/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 2,20,000/-

3 . Conventional Heads 33,000/-
 Total 23,32,000/-
11.

Consequently, the claimants would be entitled for compensation of Rs.23,32,000/- as against Rs.12,85,000/- awarded by the Tribunal, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
12. The K.S.R.T.C. is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
